key_insight: X-AgentRed automatically discovers harmful cross-service tool sequences by building and evolving a dependency graph from tool effects and preconditions, rather than relying on fixed prompt-based red-teaming.
engineering_relevance: This improves safety testing for personal agents that act across multiple services, helping expose risky emergent failures before deployment.
method: Model tools as a directed graph where one tool’s effects can satisfy another tool’s preconditions.
Sample tool-call recipes from the graph and instantiate them as realistic red-teaming scenarios.
Use execution feedback to refine blocked preconditions and diversify harmful paths through tool substitution.
evidence_signal: Across four frontier agentic models, the method achieved 1.77× the harmful path rate of STAC and 2.99× average tool coverage.
watch_item: Because it relies on execution feedback and evolving tool graphs, results may depend on the completeness and fidelity of tool descriptions, preconditions, and environment simulation.
paper_title: X-AgentRed: Red-Teaming Personal Agents in Evolving Multi-Service Ecosystems
